plain_english_policy: HB680 (2013) is a permissive expansion of firearm access in Alabama’s K-12 schools. It creates a new class of armed personnel—school security officers—and explicitly carves out exceptions to state gun-free school laws for them, while shifting training costs to the state.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The bill would shift Alabama’s approach toward arming school staff from a restrictive model (where only law enforcement or licensed concealed carriers could carry firearms on campus) to a more permissive one. It institutionalizes an armed security presence in schools by allowing local boards of education to designate employees as ‘school security personnel’ and equip them with firearms under specific conditions. This policy direction reflects a broader trend toward arming school staff (often called ‘School Resource Officers’ or SROs) to enhance security, though it does not mandate universal arming—it grants discretionary authority to local boards.

evidence_quotes: A local board of education may designate employees as school security personnel. A local board of education may allow any person employed by the board as school security personnel to carry a firearm while on duty if the employee satisfies all of the following qualifications:

(e) School security personnel qualified under subsection (a) of Section 1 of the act amending this subsection, employed by a local board of education, and authorized by the employing local board of education to carry a deadly weapon while on duty are exempt from subsection (c) of this section.

The State Department of Education shall pay all expenses associated with a designated employee's completion of the qualification requirements in subsection (a), including any time off from employment to complete training.
